Engine's answer, Excel to be asked: with a future value. Every evaluation in an x87's 64 bits that gives PMT-001 to 008 gives this double, as the engine's exact payment rounded once does; the evaluations that carry (1+rate)^n-1 in excess forms give six others, a few units in the last place away (spikes/exsheet-financial-evaluation/, --spread)

Engine's answer, Excel to be asked: with a future value. The evaluations that give PMT-001 to 008 part here, the 64-bit ones among themselves: the engine's exact payment rounded once and 266 of the 304 in an x87's 64 bits give this double, the other 38 give -20936.487788661154, one unit in the last place away, and the excess forms others (spikes/exsheet-financial-evaluation/, --spread)

Engine's answer, Excel to be asked: at a small rate the evaluations that give PMT-001 to 008 part widely, because an x87's 1+rate keeps only the rate's bits above 2^-64. The 304 in an x87's 64 bits give nine doubles across 3390 units in the last place, differing from the 13th significant digit (-83.33338750000993 to -83.33338750005811); the engine's exact payment rounded once is the first of them (spikes/exsheet-financial-evaluation/, --spread)

Engine's answer, Excel to be asked: a daily rate over a year. The 304 evaluations in an x87's 64 bits that give PMT-001 to 008 give four doubles across 7 units in the last place, and all 2504 that give them nine across 12; the engine's exact payment rounded once is one of the four (spikes/exsheet-financial-evaluation/, --spread)
